subject: Private Offer: CloudNova funding window, pricing tiers & buyer approval path
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena@cloudnova.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-14T08:23:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private offer inquiry — term & approval timing

Jordan —

Thanks for the quick demo last week. Procurement here at CloudNova is preparing to move forward but we have two constraints that matter for our CFO signoff: a shorter funded window (we can only commit cash on a 6-month cadence right now) and a clear buyer-approval roster so legal/procurement know who needs to sign.

Can Redwood provide (a) a 6-month private offer pricing row (we'd accept an annual-equivalent price prorated for 6 months) and (b) confirmation of the seller acceptance window — our procurement must see the offer for at least 7 business days before final signature to align with internal review cycles.

Also attaching the SOW and rough usage forecast for the pilot. Can you loop in finance and legal if there are any nonstandard clauses?

—Elena

Attachments: CloudNova-SOW-draft.pdf (application/pdf), cloudnova-forecast.csv (spreadsheet stub)
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@cloudnova.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, AWS Marketplace Sales <aws-mkt-sales@amazon.com>
Date: 2027-05-14T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private offer inquiry — term & approval timing

Elena —

Appreciate the clarity. Summary of what Redwood can do and next steps:

- Term/pricing: we can create a 6-month private offer that mirrors our 12-month unit pricing but with a small premium (we propose +8% effective APR over the annual rate) to account for shorter commitment. I attached a quick 6mo vs 12mo pricing model.
- Seller acceptance window: we can set the AWS private-offer window to 10 business days (meets your 7-day requirement and gives time for AWS listing acceptance).
- Approver roster: confirm the buyer role list you need — CFO + Procurement Director is standard; we can also include a delegated approver clause for procurement to sign on behalf of the CFO within the window.
- Legal: Redwood legal is comfortable with the SOW except we flagged a data-retention clause; Soojin will confirm any redline.

Next steps: (1) Redwood to send private-offer draft in AWS with 6-mo pricing row and 10-business-day seller acceptance window, (2) CloudNova to validate approver roster and return SOW redlines, (3) we coordinate with AWS contact (cc'd) to publish the private offer once both sides sign off.

I will loop in Soojin and Karthik for approvals. If that all works, we can target offer live by end of week.

Thanks —
Jordan

Attachments: cloudnova-pricing-model-6mo-vs-12mo.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-15T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private offer inquiry — term & approval timing

Jordan / Karthik —

Quick internal on approvals and risk:

- Finance (Karthik) needs to confirm the revenue recognition treatment for a 6-month upfront payment; if CloudNova pays the full 6-mo invoice up front we recognize differently than monthly. Karthik, please confirm if the +8% premium meets our ARR threshold or if we need to adjust.
- Legal: I checked the SOW — the only nonstandard item is the data-retention clause Elena flagged. Suggest replacing the broad language with a 90-day retention default and business-critical logs held for 1 year, subject to an addendum for regulated workloads.
- Buyer approvals: to avoid delays, include a procurement-delegation line in the private offer that allows a named procurement approver to accept on behalf of the CFO within the 10-business-day seller window. This is common and AWS will accept the delegation language.

I am OK with pushing the private-offer draft to AWS once Karthik confirms the revenue side. If finance asks for a different premium, suggest Jordan hold a quick call with CloudNova CFO to explain tradeoffs.

—Soojin
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@cloudnova.com>, Procurement <procurement@cloudnova.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, AWS Marketplace Sales <aws-mkt-sales@amazon.com>
Date: 2027-05-17T16:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private offer inquiry — term & approval timing

Elena / Procurement team —

Thanks for confirming the internal signers on your side (you listed: Maria Chen, CFO; Miguel Torres, Procurement Director; and Ana Ruiz, delegated procurement lead). Per our internal check:

- Redwood will publish a 6-month private offer row priced at the annual list prorated with an 8% premium.
- Seller acceptance window set to 10 business days.
- Private-offer wording will include a delegation clause allowing Miguel or Ana to accept on behalf of Maria if Maria provides written delegation prior to the offer date.
- Legal redline: we will replace the broad retention clause with the proposed 90-day default + 1-year critical logs.

I've created the private offer draft in AWS (link below). Please confirm you have visibility and that the approver emails are correct. Once you confirm, AWS will require seller acceptance to go live — AWS team, please advise estimated processing SLA after seller acceptance.

Link to draft: https://aws.amazon.com/marketplace/private-offer/draft/abc123
HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.example.com/deal/78921

If everything looks good, aim to accept by 2027-05-21 to stay within procurement funding runs.

Best —
Jordan
